bibl.title: Cell-type-specific plasticity of inhibitory interneurons in the rehabilitation of auditory cortex after peripheral damage

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: how compensatory cortical plasticity IS IMPLEMENTED AND DISTRIBUTED OVER A DIVERSE COLLECTION OF EXCITATORY AND INHIBITORY CORTICAL NEURONS
span.quote: Peripheral sensory organ damage leads to compensatory cortical plasticity that is associated with a remarkable recovery of cortical responses to sound. The precise mechanisms that explain how this plasticity is implemented and distributed over a diverse collection of excitatory and inhibitory cortical neurons remain unknown. After noise trauma and persistent peripheral deficits, we found recovered sound-evoked activity in mouse A1 excitatory principal neurons (PNs), parvalbumin- and vasoactive intestinal peptide-expressing neurons (PVs and VIPs), but reduced activity in somatostatin-expressing neurons (SOMs). This cell-type-specific recovery was also associated with cell-type-specific intrinsic plasticity. These findings, along with our computational modelling results, are consistent with the notion that PV plasticity contributes to PN stability, SOM plasticity allows for increased PN and PV activity, and VIP plasticity enables PN and PV recovery by inhibiting SOMs.

span.label: which interneuron subtypes change during cortical recovery, given that DESPITE THE ESTABLISHED ROLE OF REDUCED GABAERGIC SIGNALING IN A1 PLASTICITY AFTER COCHLEAR DAMAGE, THE PLASTICITY OF DIFFERENT IN SUBTYPES IN CORTICAL RECOVERY REMAINED UNKNOWN
span.quote: This distinct, cell-type-specific plasticity supports the notion that PVs, SOMs, and VIPs play distinct roles in cortical recovery after peripheral damage. Namely, after noise trauma, we found enhanced sound-evoked activity in PNs (Fig. 2 ), PVs (Fig. 4 ), and VIPs (Fig. 8 ) but reduced sound-evoked activity in SOMs

span.label: RECOVERED SOUND-EVOKED ACTIVITY IN mouse A1 PNs, PVs AND VIPs, BUT REDUCED ACTIVITY IN SOMs - a cell-type-specific split, with a proposed division of labor built on it
span.quote: Peripheral sensory organ damage leads to compensatory cortical plasticity that is associated with a remarkable recovery of cortical responses to sound. The precise mechanisms that explain how this plasticity is implemented and distributed over a diverse collection of excitatory and inhibitory cortical neurons remain unknown. After noise trauma and persistent peripheral deficits, we found recovered sound-evoked activity in mouse A1 excitatory principal neurons (PNs), parvalbumin- and vasoactive intestinal peptide-expressing neurons (PVs and VIPs), but reduced activity in somatostatin-expressing neurons (SOMs). This cell-type-specific recovery was also associated with cell-type-specific intrinsic plasticity. These findings, along with our computational modelling results, are consistent with the notion that PV plasticity contributes to PN stability, SOM plasticity allows for increased PN and PV activity, and VIP plasticity enables PN and PV recovery by inhibiting SOMs.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: These findings, along with our computational modelling results, are consistent with the notion that PV plasticity contributes to PN stability, SOM plasticity allows for increased PN and PV activity, and VIP plasticity enables PN and PV recovery by inhibiting SOMs.

span.label: compensatory auditory cortical plasticity after cochlear damage
span.quote: Peripheral sensory organ damage leads to compensatory cortical plasticity that is associated with a remarkable recovery of cortical responses to sound.

span.label: in-vivo-imaging-electrophysiology-and-simulation
span.quote: We employed electrophysiological and immunohistochemical assays to assess peripheral damage, longitudinal in vivo two-photon (2P) calcium imaging to assess the activity of different cortical neuronal subtypes, ex vivo electrophysiology assays to assess cellular excitability of different cortical neuronal subtypes, and computational models to shape our hypotheses and predictions.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Robust VIP firing suppresses somatostatin interneurons, and that loss of somatostatin inhibition disinhibits principal and parvalbumin neurons, raising their gain (the VIP to SOM to PN disinhibitory pathway)
span.quote: The VIP → SOM → PN disinhibitory pathway completes the task, whereby robust VIP activity enables reduced SOM activity.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Withdrawal of somatostatin-mediated inhibition is what permits the increased parvalbumin and principal-neuron gain after damage
span.quote: Moreover, the vastly decreased SOM activity allows for increased PV and PN gain, which supports stability and high gain.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Raised principal-neuron gain feeds excitation forward onto parvalbumin neurons, whose increased firing then holds the recurrently excited principal-neuron network stable
span.quote: For example, the increased PN gain via reduced SOM activity would also lead to increased PV firing because of the strong excitatory feedback from PNs to PVs.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Mutual inhibition between somatostatin and VIP populations creates a winner-take-all competition, so a small tilt toward VIP produces a large collapse in somatostatin activity
span.quote: Most notably, the strong mutual inhibition between SOMs and VIPs (Fig. 7a ; highlighted) potentially drives a competitive dynamic between these two subpopulations, where tipping the activity in favor of one subpopulation could lead to a dramatic suppression of the other subpopulation 68 .

span.label: the proposed division of labor: PV PLASTICITY CONTRIBUTES TO PN STABILITY, SOM PLASTICITY ALLOWS FOR INCREASED PN AND PV ACTIVITY, AND VIP PLASTICITY ENABLES PN AND PV RECOVERY BY INHIBITING SOMs
span.quote: Peripheral sensory organ damage leads to compensatory cortical plasticity that is associated with a remarkable recovery of cortical responses to sound. The precise mechanisms that explain how this plasticity is implemented and distributed over a diverse collection of excitatory and inhibitory cortical neurons remain unknown. After noise trauma and persistent peripheral deficits, we found recovered sound-evoked activity in mouse A1 excitatory principal neurons (PNs), parvalbumin- and vasoactive intestinal peptide-expressing neurons (PVs and VIPs), but reduced activity in somatostatin-expressing neurons (SOMs). This cell-type-specific recovery was also associated with cell-type-specific intrinsic plasticity. These findings, along with our computational modelling results, are consistent with the notion that PV plasticity contributes to PN stability, SOM plasticity allows for increased PN and PV activity, and VIP plasticity enables PN and PV recovery by inhibiting SOMs.

span.label: and the circuit it is read off, which is imported rather than measured here: BASED ON THE KNOWN SEQUENTIALLY ORGANIZED INHIBITORY CORTICAL NETWORK, WHERE VIPs NEURONS INHIBIT SOMs, SOMs INHIBIT PVs AND PNs, AND PVs INHIBIT OTHER PVs AND PNs
span.quote: Based on the known sequentially organized inhibitory cortical network 35 , where VIPs neurons inhibit SOMs, SOMs inhibit PVs and PNs, and PVs inhibit other PVs and PNs

span.label: why PVs and not another class are proposed as the stabiliser: PNs AND PVs ARE EMBEDDED INTO VERY SIMILAR SYNAPTIC ENVIRONMENTS, and THIS SYMMETRY PLACES PVs IN A STRATEGIC POSITION FOR MONITORING AND STABILIZING PN ACTIVITY
span.quote: PNs and PVs are embedded into very similar synaptic environments. Both receive the excitatory drive from upstream areas 35 , 36 , and both receive strong recurrent excitation, as well as PV- and SOM-mediated inhibition 66 . This symmetry places PVs in a strategic position for monitoring and stabilizing PN activity

span.label: the same reduction proposed as a general rule: THE REDUCED CORTICAL SOM ACTIVITY AFTER PERIPHERAL ORGAN DAMAGE MAY BE A COMMON MECHANISM ACROSS SENSORY CORTICES THAT PERMITS THE INCREASED PN GAIN
span.quote: Together, these results suggest that the reduced cortical SOM activity after peripheral organ damage may be a common mechanism across sensory cortices that permits the increased PN gain.

span.label: and an intrinsic component beside the synaptic one: THE CELL-TYPE-SPECIFIC INTRINSIC PLASTICITY FOUND IN PVs AND VIPs, BUT NOT IN EITHER PNs OR SOMs, are CONSISTENT WITH CONTRIBUTIONS OF INTRINSIC PLASTICITY MECHANISMS IN CORTICAL RECOVERY
span.quote: However, it is also clear that in addition to synaptic mechanisms, the cell-type-specific intrinsic plasticity found in PVs 31 and VIPs (Fig. 9 ), but not in either PNs 31 or SOMs (Fig. 5 ), are consistent with contributions of intrinsic plasticity mechanisms in cortical recovery.

span.label: The proposed causal roles of PV, SOM and VIP neurons in cortical recovery were not experimentally tested.
span.note: what this limits: the causal roles of PV, SOM and VIP: THE CAUSALITY OR EVEN THE CONTRIBUTION OF THE PROPOSED ROLES ... WERE NOT TESTED HERE
span.quote: Although the causality or even the contribution of the proposed roles of PVs, SOMs, and VIPs and recovered A1 sound processing were not tested here, they will be evaluated in future work.

span.label: The four cell classes studied are not homogeneous populations.
span.note: what this limits: every cell-class result: THESE NEURONAL SUBTYPES ARE NOT A HOMOGENEOUS POPULATION
span.quote: In this context, one limitation of our study is that we studied cellular mechanisms based on distinguishing PNs, PVs, SOMs, and VIPs; however, these neuronal subtypes are not a homogeneous population 35 , 36 .

span.label: Two-photon imaging sampled only layer 2/3.
span.note: what this limits: the imaging results: OUR 2P STUDIES WERE ONLY LIMITED TO L2/3
span.quote: Moreover, our 2P studies were only limited to L2/3.

span.label: No direct measure of network stability was obtained, despite stability being central to the proposed mechanism.
span.note: what this limits: the stability account: ALTHOUGH WE DO NOT PRESENT A MEASURE OF NETWORK STABILITY - the concept the mechanism rests on is not measured
span.quote: Although we do not present a measure of network stability, future studies could utilize optogenetic perturbations to further investigate our proposed roles of PVs, SOMs, and VIPs while also evaluating how network stability changes after NIHL.

span.label: Subcortical contributions to recovery were outside the study's scope.
span.note: what this limits: the attribution of recovery to cortex: THE RECOVERY OF CORTICAL SOUND PROCESSING AFTER NOISE TRAUMA IS INFLUENCED BY SUBCORTICAL PLASTICITY MECHANISMS, WHICH ARE ALSO OUTSIDE THE SCOPE OF THIS STUDY
span.quote: Moreover, we are aware that the recovery of cortical sound processing after noise trauma is influenced by subcortical plasticity mechanisms 10 , 32 , which are also outside the scope of this study.

span.label: the paper's central claim is declared untested in its own discussion: ALTHOUGH THE CAUSALITY OR EVEN THE CONTRIBUTION OF THE PROPOSED ROLES OF PVs, SOMs, AND VIPs AND RECOVERED A1 SOUND PROCESSING WERE NOT TESTED HERE, THEY WILL BE EVALUATED IN FUTURE WORK
span.note: what this limits: reading the division of labor as a measured mechanism rather than as an account consistent with the measured activity changes
span.quote: Although the causality or even the contribution of the proposed roles of PVs, SOMs, and VIPs and recovered A1 sound processing were not tested here, they will be evaluated in future work.

span.label: and again for the quantity the argument turns on - ALTHOUGH WE DO NOT PRESENT A MEASURE OF NETWORK STABILITY, FUTURE STUDIES COULD UTILIZE OPTOGENETIC PERTURBATIONS TO FURTHER INVESTIGATE OUR PROPOSED ROLES
span.note: what this limits: any use of the words `stabiliser` and `stability` in this record, which name a quantity the paper did not measure
span.quote: Although we do not present a measure of network stability, future studies could utilize optogenetic perturbations to further investigate our proposed roles of PVs, SOMs, and VIPs while also evaluating how network stability changes after NIHL.

span.label: and a third time, in the sentence that states the conclusion - OUR OBSERVATIONS ARE CONSISTENT WITH THE NOTION, ALBEIT NOT TESTED HERE, THAT PVs ACT AS THE STABILIZERS, WHEREAS SOMs ACT AS THE MODULATORS OF A1 PLASTICITY
span.note: what this limits: the paper's central conclusion: OUR OBSERVATIONS ARE CONSISTENT WITH THE NOTION, ALBEIT NOT TESTED HERE, THAT PVs ACT AS THE STABILIZERS, WHEREAS SOMs ACT AS THE MODULATORS
span.quote: Taken together, our observations are consistent with the notion, albeit not tested here, that PVs act as the stabilizers, whereas SOMs act as the modulators of A1 plasticity.

span.label: THE MODEL'S OWN MECHANISM WAS LOOKED FOR AND NOT FOUND: WE MODELED RECOVERY AS EITHER DEPOLARIZATION OR HYPERPOLARIZATION OF THE RESTING MEMBRANE POTENTIAL INDUCED BY CURRENT INJECTION - HOWEVER, OUR RESULTS DID NOT SHOW A CHANGE IN RESTING MEMBRANE POTENTIAL AFTER NIHL
span.note: what this limits: reading the model's recovery variable as the biological one
span.quote: At the neuronal level, we modeled recovery as either depolarization or hyperpolarization of the resting membrane potential induced by current injection. After peripheral injuries, such as in NIHL, it is possible that intrinsic or synaptic mechanisms of homeostatic plasticity could lead to such changes in the membrane potential. However, our results did not show a change in resting membrane potential after NIHL.

span.label: the regime the model sits in is an assumption, and whether it holds is open - THE ASSUMPTION THAT CORTICAL INHIBITION IS NEEDED TO PREVENT PATHOLOGIC ACTIVITY PLACES THE MODEL IN THE ISN (ISN) REGIME, and IT REMAINS AN OPEN QUESTION WHETHER THE CORTEX LIES IN THE ISN REGIME
span.note: what this limits: the ISN framing: IT REMAINS AN OPEN QUESTION WHETHER THE CORTEX LIES IN THE ISN REGIME WITH INHIBITION ACTIVELY PREVENTING UNSTABLE DYNAMICS OR IS SIMPLY WIRED TO RESIST INSTABILITY
span.quote: However, it remains an open question whether the cortex lies in the ISN regime with inhibition actively preventing unstable dynamics by balancing excitation or is simply wired to resist instability.

span.label: THE NEURONAL SUBTYPES ARE NOT A HOMOGENEOUS POPULATION, and OUR 2P STUDIES WERE ONLY LIMITED TO L2/3
span.note: what this limits: reading `PV`, `SOM` and `VIP` in this record as the whole class rather than the layer-2/3 members labeled by one line
span.quote: In this context, one limitation of our study is that we studied cellular mechanisms based on distinguishing PNs, PVs, SOMs, and VIPs; however, these neuronal subtypes are not a homogeneous population 35 , 36 . Moreover, our 2P studies were only limited to L2/3.

span.label: THE RECOVERY OF CORTICAL SOUND PROCESSING AFTER NOISE TRAUMA IS INFLUENCED BY SUBCORTICAL PLASTICITY MECHANISMS, WHICH ARE ALSO OUTSIDE THE SCOPE OF THIS STUDY
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 4 - subcortical plasticity is outside the study
span.quote: Moreover, we are aware that the recovery of cortical sound processing after noise trauma is influenced by subcortical plasticity mechanisms 10 , 32 , which are also outside the scope of this study.

span.label: the two imaging methods do not agree in size - WIDE-FIELD IMAGING SHOWED LARGER SHIFTS AND REDUCED RECOVERY IN THE RESPONSE THRESHOLDS COMPARED TO THE 2P IMAGING, because WIDE-FIELD IMAGING ASSESSES RESPONSES FROM DIFFERENT NEURONAL COMPARTMENTS AND DIFFERENT CORTICAL LAYERS, WHEREAS 2P IMAGING ASSESSES ONLY L2/3 SOMATIC RESPONSES
span.note: what this limits: comparing a threshold shift from this paper against one measured by the other method
span.quote: Although we found overall similar plasticity rules via 2P and wide-field imaging after NIHL, wide-field imaging showed larger shifts and reduced recovery in the response thresholds compared to the 2P imaging. The main reason that likely explains these differences is that wide-field imaging assesses responses from different neuronal compartments (somata and dendrites) and different cortical layers, whereas 2P imaging assesses only L2/ 3 somatic responses

span.label: the recovery does not restore what matters most - COMPENSATORY A1 PLASTICITY LIKELY SUPPORTS THE RECOVERY OF THE PERCEPTUAL SOUND-DETECTION THRESHOLD BUT DOES NOT SUPPORT SOUND PROCESSING ENCODED BY PRECISE SPIKE TIMING, SUCH AS MODULATED NOISE OR SPEECH, AND RESTRICTS HEARING IN A NOISY ENVIRONMENT
span.note: what this limits: what the measured recovery covers: COMPENSATORY A1 PLASTICITY LIKELY SUPPORTS THE RECOVERY OF THE PERCEPTUAL SOUND-DETECTION THRESHOLD BUT DOES NOT SUPPORT SOUND PROCESSING ENCODED BY PRECISE SPIKE TIMING
span.quote: Compensatory A1 plasticity after peripheral damage likely supports the recovery of the perceptual sound-detection threshold but does not support sound processing encoded by precise spike timing, such as modulated noise or speech, and restricts hearing in a noisy environment

span.label: and the proposed link to that deficit is flagged as untested too - BASED ON THESE RESULTS AND ALTHOUGH NOT TESTED HERE, WE PROPOSE THAT THE REDUCED SOM ACTIVITY AFTER COCHLEAR DAMAGE MAY CONTRIBUTE TO THE HEARING PROBLEMS AFTER PERIPHERAL DAMAGE
span.note: what this limits: the link to human hearing difficulty: BASED ON THESE RESULTS AND ALTHOUGH NOT TESTED HERE, WE PROPOSE THAT THE REDUCED SOM ACTIVITY AFTER COCHLEAR DAMAGE MAY CONTRIBUTE TO THE HEARING PROBLEMS
span.quote: Based on these results and although not tested here, we propose that the reduced SOM activity after cochlear damage may contribute to the hearing problems after peripheral damage, such as difficulty in understanding speech and trouble hearing in noisy environments.

span.label: the same circuit account and its causal test - IN THE SOMATOSENSORY CORTEX, INCREASED VIP ACTIVITY FACILITATES INCREASED PN ACTIVITY IN A MOUSE MODEL OF NEUROPATHIC PAIN
span.quote: Similarly, our proposed role of VIPs as the enablers of A1 plasticity after NIHL is consistent with previous reports showing that VIPs enable cortical plasticity across the sensory cortices 68 , 77 , 80 , 81 , 83 – 85 . In the visual cortex, synaptic transmission from VIPs to SOMs is necessary and sufficient for the increased cortical responses in PNs after monocular deprivation in adult mice 80 . In the somatosensory cortex, increased VIP activity facilitates increased PN activity in a mouse model of neuropathic pain

span.label: the INHIBITION-STABILIZED NETWORK (ISN) REGIME, which the model is placed in by THE ASSUMPTION THAT CORTICAL INHIBITION IS NEEDED TO PREVENT PATHOLOGIC ACTIVITY
span.quote: The computational model assumes that after NIHL, the network must balance recovery and stabilization. The assumption that cortical inhibition is needed to prevent pathologic activity places the model in the inhibition-stabilized network (ISN) regime

span.label: a sham group put through every step of the procedure except the sound
span.quote: We did not observe any changes in sham-exposed mice, which underwent identical procedures but without the presentation of sound

span.label: the hair cells counted, not only the thresholds measured
span.quote: We found that noise exposure significantly reduced the number of ribbon synapses per IHC in the high-frequency region (16–32 kHz) of the cochlea (Fig. 1l, m ), without affecting the survival of either IHCs or OHCs

span.label: the same measurement made with two imaging methods that sample different compartments
span.quote: Although we found overall similar plasticity rules via 2P and wide-field imaging after NIHL, wide-field imaging showed larger shifts and reduced recovery in the response thresholds compared to the 2P imaging. The main reason that likely explains these differences is that wide-field imaging assesses responses from different neuronal compartments (somata and dendrites) and different cortical layers, whereas 2P imaging assesses only L2/ 3 somatic responses

span.label: the alternative recovery pathways the model permits, checked against the data
span.quote: Yet, the absence of such pathways in our experimental results implies that the dynamics observed in the ISN regime constrain the mechanisms utilized in recovery.

span.label: PV
span.quote: Our results suggest that the increased PV sound-evoked activity 10 days after NIHL (Fig. 4d, k , cyan) may stabilize the increased PN activity (Fig. 2 ). However, 1 day after NIHL, we observed reduced sound-evoked PV activity

span.label: NIHL
span.quote: Our results suggest that the increased PV sound-evoked activity 10 days after NIHL (Fig. 4d, k , cyan) may stabilize the increased PN activity (Fig. 2 ). However, 1 day after NIHL, we observed reduced sound-evoked PV activity

span.label: PVs → PN activity
span.note: SIMILARITY AS THE PREMISE OF A FUNCTIONAL ROLE: PNs and PVs sit in very similar synaptic environments - both receive upstream excitatory drive, both receive strong recurrent excitation and PV- and SOM-mediated inhibition - and THIS SYMMETRY is what places PVs in a strategic position for MONITORING AND STABILIZING PN activity. The schema has `same-as` for identity and `contrasted-with` for opposition, and nothing for 'alike enough that one can regulate the other'.
span.quote: PNs and PVs are embedded into very similar synaptic environments. Both receive the excitatory drive from upstream areas 35 , 36 , and both receive strong recurrent excitation, as well as PV- and SOM-mediated inhibition 66 . This symmetry places PVs in a strategic position for monitoring and stabilizing PN activity

span.label: THE HEADLINE MECHANISM IS DECLARED UNTESTED, IN THE PAPER'S OWN DISCUSSION: ALTHOUGH THE CAUSALITY OR EVEN THE CONTRIBUTION OF THE PROPOSED ROLES OF PVs, SOMs, AND VIPs AND RECOVERED A1 SOUND PROCESSING WERE NOT TESTED HERE, THEY WILL BE EVALUATED IN FUTURE WORK
span.quote: Although the causality or even the contribution of the proposed roles of PVs, SOMs, and VIPs and recovered A1 sound processing were not tested here, they will be evaluated in future work.

span.label: a second time, for the quantity the argument rests on: ALTHOUGH WE DO NOT PRESENT A MEASURE OF NETWORK STABILITY - and `stabilizer` is the role the paper assigns to PVs
span.quote: Although we do not present a measure of network stability, future studies could utilize optogenetic perturbations to further investigate our proposed roles of PVs, SOMs, and VIPs while also evaluating how network stability changes after NIHL.

span.label: and a third time, inside the sentence that states the conclusion: OUR OBSERVATIONS ARE CONSISTENT WITH THE NOTION, ALBEIT NOT TESTED HERE, THAT PVs ACT AS THE STABILIZERS, WHEREAS SOMs ACT AS THE MODULATORS OF A1 PLASTICITY. Three declarations of the same limit, in three places, on the claim the title carries
span.quote: Taken together, our observations are consistent with the notion, albeit not tested here, that PVs act as the stabilizers, whereas SOMs act as the modulators of A1 plasticity.

span.label: THE MODEL'S OWN MECHANISM WAS LOOKED FOR AND NOT FOUND: WE MODELED RECOVERY AS EITHER DEPOLARIZATION OR HYPERPOLARIZATION OF THE RESTING MEMBRANE POTENTIAL INDUCED BY CURRENT INJECTION - HOWEVER, OUR RESULTS DID NOT SHOW A CHANGE IN RESTING MEMBRANE POTENTIAL AFTER NIHL. The model's variable is not the measured one, and the paper says so
span.quote: At the neuronal level, we modeled recovery as either depolarization or hyperpolarization of the resting membrane potential induced by current injection. After peripheral injuries, such as in NIHL, it is possible that intrinsic or synaptic mechanisms of homeostatic plasticity could lead to such changes in the membrane potential. However, our results did not show a change in resting membrane potential after NIHL.

span.label: and the regime that makes the model's conclusions follow is an assumption whose truth is open: THE ASSUMPTION THAT CORTICAL INHIBITION IS NEEDED TO PREVENT PATHOLOGIC ACTIVITY PLACES THE MODEL IN THE ISN (ISN) REGIME, and IT REMAINS AN OPEN QUESTION WHETHER THE CORTEX LIES IN THE ISN REGIME WITH INHIBITION ACTIVELY PREVENTING UNSTABLE DYNAMICS BY BALANCING EXCITATION OR IS SIMPLY WIRED TO RESIST INSTABILITY
span.quote: However, it remains an open question whether the cortex lies in the ISN regime with inhibition actively preventing unstable dynamics by balancing excitation or is simply wired to resist instability.

span.label: AN ABSENCE USED AS A CONSTRAINT: THE ABSENCE OF SUCH PATHWAYS IN OUR EXPERIMENTAL RESULTS IMPLIES THAT THE DYNAMICS OBSERVED IN THE ISN REGIME CONSTRAIN THE MECHANISMS UTILIZED IN RECOVERY - the alternatives the model allows were not seen, and that is the argument
span.quote: Yet, the absence of such pathways in our experimental results implies that the dynamics observed in the ISN regime constrain the mechanisms utilized in recovery.

span.label: THE SAME CELL TYPE, OPPOSITE SIGN AT TWO TIMES: THE INCREASED PV SOUND-EVOKED ACTIVITY 10 DAYS AFTER NIHL MAY STABILIZE THE INCREASED PN ACTIVITY - HOWEVER, 1 DAY AFTER NIHL, WE OBSERVED REDUCED SOUND-EVOKED PV ACTIVITY. A tag reading `PV activity increases after noise trauma` is true of one time point and false of the other
span.quote: Our results suggest that the increased PV sound-evoked activity 10 days after NIHL (Fig. 4d, k , cyan) may stabilize the increased PN activity (Fig. 2 ). However, 1 day after NIHL, we observed reduced sound-evoked PV activity

span.label: and the early reduction is given a role of its own: SINCE PVs INITIATE CORTICAL PLASTICITY IN JUVENILE AND ADULT BRAIN, AN INITIAL REDUCTION IN PV ACTIVITY AFTER NIHL MAY INITIATE CORTICAL PLASTICITY - so the two signs are two stages, not a contradiction
span.quote: Since PVs initiate cortical plasticity in juvenile and adult brain 83 an initial reduction in PV activity after NIHL may initiate cortical plasticity. Consistent with this notion, a rapid drop in PV-mediated PN inhibition as early as 1 day after cochlear denervation precedes the recovery of cortical sound processing

span.label: A DISAGREEMENT WITH THREE CANDIDATE CAUSES NAMED, AND ONE OF THEM IS THE SAMPLE SIZE: a recent study REPORTED THAT THE PV SOUND-EVOKED ACTIVITY WAS REDUCED AFTER COCHLEAR DENERVATION AND REMAINED REDUCED FOR TWO WEEKS - the differences offered are the damage model (OUABAIN, WHICH ELIMINATES ~95% OF THE TYPE 1 SGNs), THE SOUND-STIMULI USED (BROADBAND VS. 12 kHz PURE TONES) AND THE NUMBER OF PVs TRACKED (82 VS. 29)
span.quote: A recent study 11 reported that the PV sound-evoked activity was reduced after cochlear denervation and remained reduced for two weeks. However, unlike our model of noise-induced cochlear damage, cochlear denervation was induced with bilateral cochlear application of ouabain, which eliminates ~95% of the type 1 SGNs. Since the type and the severity of peripheral organ damage may result in heterogeneous cortical plasticity 7 , 10 , 16 , 21 , 30 , 93 – 99 , noise- and ouabain-induced damage to the cochlea may trigger different trajectories of plasticity in A1 neuronal subtypes. Another explanation for the observed differences could arise from differences in the experimental design, such as the sound-stimuli used (broadband vs. 12 kHz pure tones 11 ) and the number of PVs tracked (82 vs. 29 11 ).

span.label: TWO IMAGING METHODS, SAME RULE, DIFFERENT SIZE: WIDE-FIELD IMAGING SHOWED LARGER SHIFTS AND REDUCED RECOVERY IN THE RESPONSE THRESHOLDS COMPARED TO THE 2P IMAGING, because WIDE-FIELD IMAGING ASSESSES RESPONSES FROM DIFFERENT NEURONAL COMPARTMENTS (SOMATA AND DENDRITES) AND DIFFERENT CORTICAL LAYERS
span.quote: Although we found overall similar plasticity rules via 2P and wide-field imaging after NIHL, wide-field imaging showed larger shifts and reduced recovery in the response thresholds compared to the 2P imaging. The main reason that likely explains these differences is that wide-field imaging assesses responses from different neuronal compartments (somata and dendrites) and different cortical layers, whereas 2P imaging assesses only L2/ 3 somatic responses

span.label: THE CLASS NAMES ARE NOT THE CLASSES: ONE LIMITATION OF OUR STUDY IS THAT WE STUDIED CELLULAR MECHANISMS BASED ON DISTINGUISHING PNs, PVs, SOMs, AND VIPs - HOWEVER, THESE NEURONAL SUBTYPES ARE NOT A HOMOGENEOUS POPULATION
span.quote: In this context, one limitation of our study is that we studied cellular mechanisms based on distinguishing PNs, PVs, SOMs, and VIPs; however, these neuronal subtypes are not a homogeneous population 35 , 36 . Moreover, our 2P studies were only limited to L2/3.

span.label: WHAT RECOVERS IS NOT WHAT MATTERS: COMPENSATORY A1 PLASTICITY LIKELY SUPPORTS THE RECOVERY OF THE PERCEPTUAL SOUND-DETECTION THRESHOLD BUT DOES NOT SUPPORT SOUND PROCESSING ENCODED BY PRECISE SPIKE TIMING, SUCH AS MODULATED NOISE OR SPEECH, AND RESTRICTS HEARING IN A NOISY ENVIRONMENT
span.quote: Compensatory A1 plasticity after peripheral damage likely supports the recovery of the perceptual sound-detection threshold but does not support sound processing encoded by precise spike timing, such as modulated noise or speech, and restricts hearing in a noisy environment

span.label: and the cell that carries that ability is the one that goes down: A1 SOMs, WHICH ARE CRITICALLY IMPORTANT FOR SOUND PROCESSING ENCODED BY PRECISE SPIKE TIMING OF NEURONAL FIRING, SHOWED REDUCED SOUND-EVOKED ACTIVITY AFTER NIHL
span.quote: Interestingly, A1 SOMs, which are critically important for sound processing encoded by precise spike timing of neuronal firing 38 , 46 , 89 , 90 , showed reduced sound-evoked activity after NIHL

span.label: A COMPOSITE MEASURE WHOSE PARTS ARE NAMED: ABR THRESHOLD AND GAIN REPRESENT THE COMBINED FUNCTIONALITY OF INNER HAIR CELLS (IHCs), OHCs, TYPE-I SGNs, AND SYNAPSES BETWEEN THE IHCs AND TYPE-I SGN DENDRITES CALLED RIBBON SYNAPSES - four things behind one number, and the paper goes on to separate them anatomically
span.quote: ABR threshold and gain represent the combined functionality of inner hair cells (IHCs), OHCs, type-I SGNs, and synapses between the IHCs and type-I SGN dendrites called ribbon synapses

span.label: and it does separate them: NOISE EXPOSURE SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCED THE NUMBER OF RIBBON SYNAPSES PER IHC IN THE HIGH-FREQUENCY REGION (16-32 kHz) OF THE COCHLEA, WITHOUT AFFECTING THE SURVIVAL OF EITHER IHCs OR OHCs
span.quote: We found that noise exposure significantly reduced the number of ribbon synapses per IHC in the high-frequency region (16–32 kHz) of the cochlea (Fig. 1l, m ), without affecting the survival of either IHCs or OHCs

span.label: THE CIRCUIT THE INTERPRETATION RESTS ON IS IMPORTED, NOT MEASURED HERE: BASED ON THE KNOWN SEQUENTIALLY ORGANIZED INHIBITORY CORTICAL NETWORK, WHERE VIPs NEURONS INHIBIT SOMs, SOMs INHIBIT PVs AND PNs, AND PVs INHIBIT OTHER PVs AND PNs
span.quote: Based on the known sequentially organized inhibitory cortical network 35 , where VIPs neurons inhibit SOMs, SOMs inhibit PVs and PNs, and PVs inhibit other PVs and PNs

span.label: membrane potential
span.quote: At the neuronal level, we modeled recovery as either depolarization or hyperpolarization of the resting membrane potential induced by current injection. After peripheral injuries, such as in NIHL, it is possible that intrinsic or synaptic mechanisms of homeostatic plasticity could lead to such changes in the membrane potential. However, our results did not show a change in resting membrane potential after NIHL.

span.label: 8–16 kHz noise at 100 dB SPL for 2 h — the noise-exposure dose used to induce hearing loss
span.quote: Mice were bilaterally exposed to an octave band (8–16 kHz) noise at 100 dB SPL for 2 h (Fig. 1a, b ).

span.label: n = 358/531 PNs from 11 mice — number of longitudinally tracked layer 2/3 principal neurons that met the sound-responsiveness criterion, out of all tracked neurons
span.quote: To identify the sound-responsive neurons, we used a tone sensitivity index ( d ’), which reflects the neurons’ selectivity for preferred frequency against non-preferred frequency 57 , 58 (“Methods”), and only the neurons with d ’ ≥ 0 were analyzed further ( n = 358/531 PNs from 11 mice).

span.label: 51.47% — proportion of viable model parameter/stimulus conditions in which somatostatin neurons received net inhibitory synaptic input after simulated damage
span.quote: Further, for a majority (51.47%) of these tested conditions, SOMs received a net inhibitory input.

span.label: F = 46.7, p = 3 × 10 −10 — effect of noise exposure on VIP firing frequency as a function of injected current, 10 days after exposure
span.quote: Although the resting membrane potential, AP width and threshold, and adaptation ratio did not change, we found increased input resistance (Fig. 9d ) and firing rate (Fig. 9j ) in VIPs from noise-exposed mice.

span.label: ~95% — share of type 1 spiral ganglion neurons eliminated by the ouabain denervation model used in a contrasting study, offered to explain differing PV results
span.quote: However, unlike our model of noise-induced cochlear damage, cochlear denervation was induced with bilateral cochlear application of ouabain, which eliminates ~95% of the type 1 SGNs.

span.label: 5000 of 100,000 — permutation-test criterion: the share of random permutations exceeding the observed mean difference that defines significance
span.quote: Samples for which 5000 of 100,000 random permutations of the data resulted in mean differences greater than the observed difference in sample means were considered significant ( p , 0.05).

span.label: 82 vs. 29 — the NUMBER OF PVs TRACKED here against the study whose result disagrees - offered as one of three candidate causes of the disagreement
span.quote: A recent study 11 reported that the PV sound-evoked activity was reduced after cochlear denervation and remained reduced for two weeks. However, unlike our model of noise-induced cochlear damage, cochlear denervation was induced with bilateral cochlear application of ouabain, which eliminates ~95% of the type 1 SGNs. Since the type and the severity of peripheral organ damage may result in heterogeneous cortical plasticity 7 , 10 , 16 , 21 , 30 , 93 – 99 , noise- and ouabain-induced damage to the cochlea may trigger different trajectories of plasticity in A1 neuronal subtypes. Another explanation for the observed differences could arise from differences in the experimental design, such as the sound-stimuli used (broadband vs. 12 kHz pure tones 11 ) and the number of PVs tracked (82 vs. 29 11 ).

span.label: ~95% — the type 1 SGNs eliminated by the OUABAIN model used in the disagreeing study, against noise trauma here

Another explanation for the observed differences could arise from differences in the experimental design, such as the sound-stimuli used (broadband vs. 12 kHz pure tones 11 ) and the number of PVs tracked (82 vs. 29 11 ).

span.label: 16-32 kHz — the cochlear region where ribbon synapses per IHC fell
span.quote: We found that noise exposure significantly reduced the number of ribbon synapses per IHC in the high-frequency region (16–32 kHz) of the cochlea (Fig. 1l, m ), without affecting the survival of either IHCs or OHCs

span.label: 8-32 kHz — the tone range whose ABR thresholds stayed elevated at 10 days
span.quote: Further, we found that noise exposure significantly increased the ABR response thresholds for 8–32 kHz tones, which remained elevated even 10 days after noise exposure (Fig. 1h–j ), suggesting persistent and widespread cochlear damage across the tested frequencies.
